what-is-cwd.headline: What is CWD and why does it compromise natural deer urine?
what-is-cwd.intro: CWD is a fatal, contagious neurodegenerative disorder affecting cervids (deer, elk, moose, reindeer). It is 100% fatal with no vaccine, treatment or cure.
what-is-cwd.body: Chronic Wasting Disease is a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy caused by misfolded proteins known as prions. Prions spread through direct contact and environmental contamination via bodily fluids such as urine, saliva, and feces. Natural deer urine is collected from captive herds. Because CWD can incubate for 18+ months without symptoms, urine from an apparently healthy herd may contain infectious prions. Distributing such products in the field risks introducing prions to new areas. State wildlife agencies therefore impose restrictions on natural cervid urine. Odin's Innovations manufactures CWD safe scents with zero animal-derived material — eliminating prion risk entirely. Odin's is legal for use in every state and in Canada.

why-odins.headline: Why Odin's Synthetic Deer Scent Outperforms Natural Urine

Odin's 100% synthetic formulations replicate targeted aromatic profiles with identical results every time. A USDA BioPreferred certified biodegradable polymer provides 30+ days of continuous release — reducing reapplication time and site disturbance.

items.question: What is CWD and why does it threaten natural deer urine products?
items.answer: Chronic Wasting Disease is a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy caused by misfolded proteins known as prions. It is always fatal in cervids — deer, elk, and moose — with no vaccine, treatment, or cure. Prions spread through direct contact and environmental contamination via bodily fluids such as urine, saliva, and feces. Natural deer urine is collected from captive herds. Because CWD can incubate for 18+ months without symptoms, urine from an apparently healthy herd may contain infectious prions. Distributing such products in the field risks introducing prions to new areas. Odin's Innovations manufactures CWD safe scents with zero animal-derived material — eliminating prion risk entirely.

items.question: Will this be the Category 2 that I am looking for?
items.answer: Odin's synthetic scent beads qualify as Category 2 compliant products in jurisdictions that categorize hunting attractants. Because they contain zero animal-derived material and hold USDA BioPreferred certification, they meet the strictest regulatory standards across all 50 states and Canada. Unlike natural urine products that face increasing restrictions due to CWD concerns, Odin's synthetic formulations provide a compliant solution regardless of local category classifications.

items.question: Are synthetic scents actually effective?
items.answer: Yes. Odin's synthetic formulations are engineered to precise molecular specifications and refined over 10+ years of field use. The 2021 acquisition of Hunter's Kloak provided a library of 21 proprietary scents now manufactured by a specialty fragrance laboratory. University laboratory testing confirmed 52% of original scent output still releasing after 27 days of continuous air exposure. The polymer releases scent molecule-by-molecule and pauses when submerged, resuming without dilution when dry.

items.question: Are Odin's products biodegradable and safe for the environment?
items.answer: Yes. Odin's synthetic scent beads use a plant-based polymer that biodegrades naturally — comparable to organic material like a banana peel — with no plastic residue. Products hold USDA BioPreferred certification through independent laboratory verification of biobased content. No unhealthy chemicals are used (DEET-free citronella option available). Rain, heavy dew, and snow do not degrade scent output.

items.question: How long does Odin's synthetic scent last?
items.answer: Scent beads provide continuous release for 30+ days. University testing showed 52% original concentration still releasing after 27 days. The polymer is unaffected by rain or snow — moisture simply pauses release without diluting the remaining scent. This reduces reapplication visits and site disturbance.

This variety would be impossible with natural urine which is limited to what can be collected from captive herds.
